condition: An event-based component has not been activated for the subscription.

provider_outcome.effect: The subscription is not billed for that component's events at renewal; activation makes renewal bill the events.

app_must: Activate each event-based component for a subscription before you expect its events to be billed.

sources.quote: To bill your subscribers on your Events data under the Events-Based Billing feature, the components must be activated for the subscriber.
Activating an event-based component causes billing for events when the subscription is renewed.

condition: The subscription is neither awaiting signup nor trialing.
app_must: Activate only awaiting-signup or trialing subscriptions.

sources.quote: Activates awaiting signup and trialing subscriptions.

condition: The site is not on the Relationship Invoicing architecture.
app_must: Use activation only on Relationship Invoicing sites.

sources.quote: This feature is only available on the Relationship Invoicing architecture.

condition: The subscription belongs to a subscription group.

provider_outcome.effect: It cannot be activated immediately.

app_must: Do not immediately activate grouped subscriptions.

sources.quote: Subscriptions in a group cannot be activated immediately.

condition: Activation fails (for example the payment fails) with revert_on_failure true.

provider_outcome.error: Purchase Declined. The subscription is now in the 'awaiting_signup' state.
provider_outcome.effect: The subscription's state and billing period do not change.

app_must: On a 400 from activation, keep the subscription's previous state and retry after fixing payment.

sources.quote: If set to `true` and something goes wrong i.e. payment fails, the subscription's state does not change. The subscription’s billing period also remains the same.
Purchase Declined. The subscription is now in the 'awaiting_signup' state.
`true` means do not change the subscription’s state and billing period.

condition: Activation fails (for example the payment fails) with revert_on_failure false.

provider_outcome.effect: Activation continues into an end-of-life state: trialing subscriptions go to trial ended (no-obligation trial), past due (trial with obligation) or canceled (no dunning strategy or cancel-immediately strategy); awaiting signup subscriptions are always canceled.

app_must: Send revert_on_failure true unless a failed activation should end the subscription.

sources.quote: If set to `false` and something goes wrong i.e. payment fails, the activation continues and enters an end of life state.

For trialing subscriptions, that is either trial ended (if the trial is no obligation), past due (if the trial has an obligation), or canceled (if the site has no dunning strategy, or has a strategy that says to cancel immediately).
For awaiting signup subscriptions, that is always canceled.

condition: revert_on_failure is omitted or null.

provider_outcome.effect: The site's Subscription Activation Settings value is used (default true).

app_must: Send revert_on_failure explicitly rather than relying on the site setting.

sources.quote: If this parameter is omitted or `null` is passed it will default to the value set in the site settings (default: `true`).
The default activation failure behavior can be configured per activation attempt, or you can set a default value under Config > Settings > Subscription Activation Settings.

condition: Activation of a trialing subscription fails with revert_on_failure true.

provider_outcome.effect: The subscription stays Trialing, the activation invoice is voided, and prepayments and credits applied to it are returned to the subscription.

app_must: Expect a voided activation invoice after a reverted trial activation.

sources.quote: When the `revert_on_failure` parameter is set to `true`, the subscription's state remains Trialing; the invoice from activation is voided, and any prepayments and credits applied to the invoice are returned to the subscription.

condition: An awaiting-signup subscription is activated successfully.

provider_outcome.effect: It moves to Trialing when the product has a trial, otherwise to Active.

app_must: Expect trialing rather than active after activation when the product has a trial.

sources.quote: A -->|Success| Active
A -->|Success| Trialing

condition: The site does not use the Relationship Billing and Customer Hierarchy features.

sources.quote: features, it is possible to add existing subscriptions to subscription groups.
features, it is possible to remove an existing subscription from a subscription group.

provider_outcome.effect: The subscription becomes a member of the target customer's subscription group.

app_must: Expect a new group, paid by the target customer, when the target is not grouped yet.

condition: The subscription to add belongs neither to the target's customer record nor to the same customer hierarchy.
app_must: Only add a subscription to a target with the same customer or within the same customer hierarchy.

sources.quote: In order to add an existing subscription to a subscription group, it must belong to either the same customer record as the target, or be within the same customer hierarchy.

condition: group.target.type is self, parent or eldest.

provider_outcome.effect: The payer is the subscribing customer (self), its parent in the hierarchy (parent) or the root customer of the hierarchy (eldest).

app_must: Pick the target type that names the intended payer; no id is needed for these types.

sources.quote: which indicates the subscription will be paid for not by some other customer, but by the subscribing customer,
which indicates the subscription will be paid for by the subscribing customer's parent within a customer hierarchy, or
which indicates the subscription will be paid for by the root-level customer in the subscribing customer's hierarchy.

condition: addSubscriptionToGroup is sent with group.billing (accrue, align_date, prorate) for an existing subscription.

provider_outcome.effect: The billing attributes apply only to new subscriptions, so they do not apply here.

condition: An allocation is made for a component that is not a Quantity, On/Off or Prepaid component (for example metered or event-based).
app_must: Allocate only Quantity, On/Off and Prepaid components; report metered usage with Create Usage.

sources.quote: Allocations can only be updated for Quantity, On/Off, and Prepaid Components.

condition: An upgrade allocation is made with accrue_charge false and the immediate charge fails.

condition: initiate_dunning is true and the immediate component payment fails.

provider_outcome.effect: Dunning is started for the subscription.

app_must: Send initiate_dunning=true only when a failed allocation payment should put the subscription into dunning.

sources.quote: If set to true, if the immediate component payment fails, initiate dunning for the subscription.
If true, if the immediate component payment fails, initiate dunning for the subscription.

condition: initiate_dunning is false or not sent and the immediate component payment fails.

condition: A decimal quantity (decimal_quantity, decimal_previous_quantity or a fractional quantity) is sent for a component without decimal allocations enabled.

condition: An allocation for an On/Off component uses a quantity other than 1 or 0.

condition: An allocation is sent without price_point_id.

app_must: Send price_point_id (id or handle) when the allocation must be charged at a non-default price point.

sources.quote: When not specified, the default price point will be used.

condition: The allocation request carries no allocation change.

provider_outcome.error: One or more allocation changes are required.

condition: proration_upgrade_scheme or proration_downgrade_scheme (deprecated) is not sent.

provider_outcome.effect: The site setting is used.

app_must: Use upgrade_charge/downgrade_credit instead of the deprecated proration schemes.

sources.quote: The scheme used if the proration is an upgrade. Defaults to the site setting if one is not provided.
The scheme used if the proration is a downgrade. Defaults to the site setting if one is not provided.

condition: An allocation was not created mid-period.

provider_outcome.effect: proration_upgrade_scheme and proration_downgrade_scheme are absent from the allocation.

condition: An allocation is returned.

provider_outcome.effect: The allocation timestamp is in UTC, while other response timestamps use the site's time zone.

conflict: Data Types says response timestamps are in the site's time zone; the Allocation schema and webhook reference say the allocation timestamp is UTC; this record follows the Allocation schema.

condition: upgrade_charge, downgrade_credit or accrue_charge is sent for a Prepaid component.

sources.quote: These proration and accrual fields are ignored for Prepaid Components since this component type always generates charges immediately without proration.

condition: A quantity-based allocation changes, an on/off component is toggled, or a prepaid allocation is purchased after signup.

provider_outcome.effect: A component_allocation_change webhook fires (allocation_change on the enhanced Catalog experience).

app_must: Handle component_allocation_change (and allocation_change) webhooks to track allocation changes.

component_allocation_change → allocation_change

Applicable only when rollover is enabled. Interval unit for rollover expiration (month or day).

app_must: Set use_default_list_price (or list_price_point_id) deliberately when overriding the customer price.

condition: upgrade_charge or downgrade_credit is resolved for an allocation.

provider_outcome.effect: The value set on the allocation wins, then the component-level default, then the top-level request value, then the site default.

Allocation API call top level (outside of the `allocations` array)

A prorated credit is added for the amount owed.

condition: A grant, debit, adjustment, purchase (or its preview) or update is sent for an archived wallet.

provider_outcome.error: Wallet is archived
provider_outcome.effect: code wallet_archived

app_must: Check the wallet's status before writing to it; archived wallets accept no further writes.

sources.quote: Archives the wallet: blocks further grants, debits, adjustments, and purchases (each returns `422`)
and an archived wallet (`wallet_archived`)
[Archive Wallet]($e/Wallets/archiveWallet) blocks further grants, debits, purchases, and adjustments

condition: A kind: debit larger than the available balance is posted to a wallet with hard_stop_overflow: allow_negative.

provider_outcome.effect: The full amount is deducted; the excess is booked as one overdraft row with grant_id null, rejected_amount is 0.0 and the balance goes negative.

app_must: Watch for negative balances on allow_negative wallets.

sources.quote: Under `hard_stop_overflow: allow_negative`, the full amount is deducted. The excess past the wallet's grants is booked as one overdraft row with `grant_id: null`, `rejected_amount` is always `"0.0"`, and the balance goes negative.

condition: A wallet amount is sent as a JSON number with a decimal point.

provider_outcome.effect: The value is rejected, never rounded; decimal strings (or whole-number integers) are accepted.

app_must: Send wallet amounts as decimal strings such as "150.0".

sources.quote: Requests follow the same rule: send amounts as decimal strings (a whole-number JSON integer is also accepted). A JSON number with a decimal point is rejected with `422`, never rounded, because it may already have lost precision before it reached the API.

condition: A debit drains several grants or goes negative.

provider_outcome.effect: One ledger row is written per grant drained, plus an overdraft row if the balance goes negative.

app_must: Expect several ledger rows from a single debit call.

sources.quote: a debit writes one row per grant it drains, plus an overdraft row if it goes negative

condition: A wallet is funded (manual grant, purchase, recurring refill or allowance increase) while its balance is negative.

provider_outcome.effect: The overdraft is repaid first (a grant row with grant_id null) and the new grant gets only what is left, possibly 0; the grant is still created with its full original.

app_must: Expect a top-up into an overdrawn wallet to show less remaining than the amount sent.

sources.quote: Any grant made while the wallet's balance is negative pays off that overdraft first
The same repay-first order applies to recurring refills, allowance increases, and purchases, since they all fund the wallet through the same mechanism as a manual grant.

condition: A debit is made against a wallet with several open grants.

provider_outcome.effect: Grants are drained earliest-expiration-first.

app_must: Expect debits to consume the soonest-expiring grants first.

sources.quote: A `debit` never carries an expiration, and drains the wallet's grants earliest-expiration-first.

condition: A kind: debit is posted to a metered wallet and live usage cannot be read in time.
app_must: Retry the debit later on 503; it is not returned for grants.

sources.quote: For a metered wallet, live usage could not be read in time to compute the debit. Not returned for `kind: grant`.

condition: For a metered wallet, usage is read but settling it against the ledger fails.
app_must: Re-read the wallet and ledger before retrying after a 500 on a metered wallet.

sources.quote: For a metered wallet, usage could be read but settling it against the ledger failed.

condition: A kind: grant is created without a memo.

provider_outcome.effect: The grant's name is set to Grant #<id>; otherwise it is the memo.

app_must: Send a memo to give the grant a readable name.

sources.quote: The memo the grant was created with, or `Grant #<id>` when none was given.

condition: createWalletTransaction is sent with an amount of 0 or less.
app_must: Always send amount positive; kind decides whether it is added or removed.

sources.quote: `amount` is always sent positive, and `kind` determines the direction written to the ledger.
a malformed, non-positive, or out-of-range `amount`

condition: A kind: grant is posted while the wallet's balance is negative.

provider_outcome.effect: The overdraft is repaid first (a grant row with grant_id null), then the grant is created with original equal to the full amount and remaining, and its row amount, equal to what is left (possibly 0).

app_must: Expect two rows and a grant whose remaining is below original when topping up an overdrawn wallet.

sources.quote: On a negative balance, it repays the overdraft first (a `kind: grant` row with `grant_id: null`, for the repaid amount), then creates the grant: its `original` is always the full `amount` sent, and its `remaining` is what's left after the overdraft was repaid
Any grant made while the wallet's balance is negative pays off that overdraft first

condition: createWalletTransaction sends expires_at with kind: debit.
app_must: Send expires_at only on grants.

sources.quote: Only accepted with `kind: grant`; sending it with `kind: debit` is rejected.
`expires_at` sent with `kind: debit`

condition: A kind: debit is posted.

provider_outcome.effect: Grants are drained earliest-expiration-first (evergreen grants last), writing one debit row per grant touched.

app_must: Expect several ledger rows from one debit and read them all.

sources.quote: direct consumption. Drains grants earliest-expiration-first, one `kind: debit` row per grant touched
Debits drain grants earliest-expiration-first (grants with no expiration are drained last).

condition: A kind: debit is posted while some grants are past their expires_at but not yet written off.

provider_outcome.effect: Those grants are expired first (kind: expiration rows), even if the debit then fails with 422 wallet_depleted.

app_must: Re-read the ledger after a failed debit; it may contain new expiration rows.

sources.quote: Before that failure is returned, this call still expires any grants that were already overdue, so a `422` response can still leave new `kind: expiration` rows written.
that failure can still leave new `kind: expiration` rows behind, from grants this same call expired before the depleted check ran.

condition: A kind: debit larger than the available balance is posted to a wallet with hard_stop_overflow: discard.

provider_outcome.effect: The drain is capped at the available balance; requested_amount, drained_amount and rejected_amount report how much was covered.

app_must: Read drained_amount and rejected_amount on every debit; a 201 does not mean the full amount was taken.

sources.quote: Under the wallet's default `hard_stop_overflow: discard`, the drain is capped at the available balance.
Under the default `hard_stop_overflow: discard`, a debit larger than the available balance is capped

condition: A kind: debit is posted to a metered discard wallet whose live usage has already consumed part or all of the stored balance.

provider_outcome.effect: The cap is the live metered balance, so the debit can drain less than the stored balance suggests, or nothing (drained_amount 0.0).

app_must: Do not assume a stored-balance check predicts how much a debit on a metered wallet will drain.

sources.quote: For a metered wallet, that cap is the live metered balance, not the stored one, so a debit can drain less than its stored balance would suggest, or even drain nothing at all (`201` with `drained_amount: "0.0"`)

condition: A kind: debit is posted to a discard wallet whose stored balance is already zero or below.

provider_outcome.error: Wallet is depleted
provider_outcome.effect: code wallet_depleted

app_must: Handle wallet_depleted as 'no units left' rather than as a malformed request.

sources.quote: A debit against a wallet whose *stored* balance is already zero or negative (`discard` only ever reaches zero) returns `422 "Wallet is depleted"`.
A debit against a wallet whose _stored_ balance is already at or below zero returns `422` rather than a zero-amount success

condition: An event-based component is deactivated for a subscription.

provider_outcome.effect: Related events are ignored at subscription renewal.

app_must: Deactivate only when the subscription should stop being billed for those events.

sources.quote: Deactivating the event-based component causes Advanced Billing to ignore related events at subscription renewal.

condition: The deduction amount is more than the subscription's current service credit balance.

provider_outcome.error: Amount cannot exceed current service credit account balance.

app_must: Read the service credit balance and deduct no more than it.

sources.quote: The credit amount being deducted must be equal to or less than the current credit balance.
Amount cannot exceed current service credit account balance.

condition: A deduction amount of 0 or less is sent.

provider_outcome.error: Amount must be greater than 0.

app_must: Send a deduction amount greater than 0.

sources.quote: Amount must be greater than 0.

condition: The subcode in the URL path contains one of the special characters % @ + - _ or . without percent-encoding.
app_must: Percent-encode % @ + - _ and . in the subcode path segment (for example 20%OFF as 20%25OFF).

sources.quote: Note: If you are using any of the allowed special characters (“%”, “@”, “+”, “-”, “_”, and “.”), you must encode them for use in the URL.
So, if the coupon subcode is `20%OFF`, the URL to delete this coupon subcode would be: `https://<subdomain>.chargify.com/coupons/567/codes/20%25OFF.<format>`.

condition: A customer is deleted explicitly as a single action.

provider_outcome.effect: A customer_delete webhook is sent; it is not sent when a subscription and its customer are deleted together.

app_must: Do not expect customer_delete when the customer is removed together with a subscription; reconcile those deletions separately.

sources.quote: This webhook is **not** triggered by the deletion of a Subscription and Customer simultaneously; it is only triggered by explicitly deleting the customer as a single action.

condition: An invoice that is not in draft status is deleted.

provider_outcome.error: Status must be draft.

app_must: Delete only draft invoices; void issued invoices instead.

sources.quote: **Important: only invoices with the `adhoc` role and `draft` status can be deleted.**
Status must be draft.
Issued invoices should be voided instead.

condition: An invoice that is not ad hoc (for example a renewal or signup invoice) is deleted.

provider_outcome.error: Only adhoc invoices can be deleted.

app_must: Delete only ad hoc invoices.

sources.quote: Only adhoc invoices can be deleted.

condition: A draft ad hoc invoice is deleted.

provider_outcome.effect: The invoice is permanently removed.

app_must: Confirm before deleting; a deleted invoice cannot be recovered.

sources.quote: A successful deletion returns a `204 No Content` response and the invoice is permanently removed.

condition: A metafield is deleted.

provider_outcome.effect: The metafield and its metadata are removed from every subscription or customer on the site.

app_must: Delete a metafield only when its values are no longer needed on any record.

sources.quote: Removes the metafield and associated metadata from all Subscriptions or Customers resources on the Site.

condition: A subscription's allocated quantity for a prepaid usage component must go down.

provider_outcome.effect: Prepaid usage allocations are always additive; the quantity can only be reduced by deleting individual allocations.

app_must: Reduce a prepaid usage component by deleting allocations one by one, not by allocating a lower quantity.

sources.quote: Prepaid Usage components are unique in that their allocations are always additive. In order to reduce a subscription's allocated quantity for a prepaid usage component, each allocation must be destroyed individually via this endpoint.

conflict: Allocate Component says it sets the current allocated quantity; Delete Prepaid Usage Allocation says prepaid allocations are always additive; this record follows Delete Prepaid Usage Allocation.

condition: A prepaid usage allocation is deleted with credit_scheme credit or without credit_scheme.

provider_outcome.effect: The allocation is destroyed, balances are updated and a service credit is generated on the subscription.

app_must: Send credit_scheme none or refund if a service credit is not wanted.

sources.quote: By default, destroying an allocation will generate a service credit on the subscription.
This is also the default behavior if the `credit_scheme` param is not passed.

conflict: Credit-Scheme-Request marks credit_scheme as required; the operation description says it is optional and defaults to credit; this record follows the description.

condition: A prepaid usage allocation is deleted with credit_scheme none.

provider_outcome.effect: The allocation is destroyed and balances are updated, but no service credit or refund is created.

app_must: Use credit_scheme none only when the customer should get nothing back.

sources.quote: `none`: The allocation will be destroyed and the balances will be updated but no service credit or refund will be created.

condition: A prepaid usage allocation is deleted with credit_scheme refund.

provider_outcome.effect: The allocation is destroyed, balances are updated, and a refund is issued along with a Credit Note.

app_must: Use credit_scheme refund when the customer must be refunded, and expect a credit note.

sources.quote: `refund`: The allocation will be destroyed and the balances will be updated and a refund will be issued along with a Credit Note.

condition: A reason code is deleted.

provider_outcome.effect: The code is removed immediately and the deletion cannot be reversed.

app_must: Confirm before deleting a reason code; recreate it if needed rather than expecting a restore.

sources.quote: Deletes a reason code from the Churn Reason Codes. This code will be immediately removed. This action is not reversible.

condition: deleteSubscriptionGroup is called on a group that still has members.
app_must: Remove all members (updateSubscriptionGroupMembers with an empty member_ids) before deleting a group.

sources.quote: Only groups without members can be deleted.

condition: The deleted payment profile belongs to several subscription groups and/or subscriptions.

provider_outcome.effect: The payment profile is removed from all of them.

app_must: Check every group and subscription that used the profile for a missing payment method after this delete.

sources.quote: **Note**: If the Payment Profile belongs to multiple Subscription Groups and/or Subscriptions, it will be removed from all of them.

condition: A payment profile is deleted through one subscription while the customer has several subscriptions.

provider_outcome.effect: The payment profile is removed from all of the customer's subscriptions.

app_must: Check every subscription of the customer for a missing payment method after this delete.

sources.quote: If the customer has multiple subscriptions, the payment profile is removed from all of them.

condition: The deleted payment profile is the subscription's default payment profile.

provider_outcome.effect: The subscription is left without a default payment profile until another is set.

app_must: Set another default payment profile through the API, or prompt the customer to add one, after deleting the default.

sources.quote: If you delete the default payment profile for a subscription, you need to specify another payment profile to be the default through the API, or either prompt the user to enter a card in the billing portal or on the self-service page

condition: The payment profile is in use by one or more subscriptions or subscription groups.

provider_outcome.error: The payment profile is in use by one or more subscriptions and cannot be deleted

app_must: Move subscriptions and groups to another payment profile before deleting this one, or use the subscription-scoped delete.

sources.quote: If the payment profile is in use by one or more subscriptions or groups, an error message is returned.
The payment profile is in use by one or more subscriptions and cannot be deleted

condition: A proforma invoice is delivered without recipient_emails.

provider_outcome.effect: It is sent to the primary recipient derived from the invoice or subscription.

app_must: Send recipient_emails when the proforma must go to someone other than the default recipient.

sources.quote: If `recipient_emails` is omitted, the system will fall back to the primary recipient derived from the invoice or subscription.

condition: No recipient is given and none can be derived from the invoice or subscription.

provider_outcome.error: recipient_emails: must include at least one email

app_must: Send at least one recipient email when the subscription has no default recipient.

sources.quote: At least one recipient must be present, either via the request body or via this default behavior, so an empty body may still succeed when defaults are available.
recipient_emails: must include at least one email

condition: A recipient email address is not valid.

provider_outcome.error: recipient_emails: must be a valid email address

app_must: Validate email addresses before delivering a proforma invoice.

sources.quote: recipient_emails: must be a valid email address

condition: The proforma invoice cannot be queued for email delivery.

provider_outcome.error: Unable to enqueue proforma invoice for email delivery

app_must: Treat this 422 as not sent and show the error rather than assuming delivery.

sources.quote: Unable to enqueue proforma invoice for email delivery

condition: Billing Portal access is enabled for a customer who already has it enabled.

provider_outcome.error: Portal is already enabled for this customer.

app_must: Check portal_customer_created_at or handle the 422 as already enabled instead of retrying.

sources.quote: - Portal is already enabled for this customer.

condition: auto_invite=1 is sent in the query when enabling the Billing Portal.

provider_outcome.effect: An invitation email is sent to the customer; with auto_invite=0 or no auto_invite, no email is sent.

app_must: Send auto_invite=1 only when the customer should receive the portal invitation email now.

sources.quote: When set to 1, an Invitation email will be sent to the Customer. When set to 0, or not sent, an email will not be sent.

condition: The customer has been invited to the Billing Portal.

provider_outcome.effect: The customer's statements, invoices and receipts automatically carry the Management URL at the bottom.

app_must: Expect invited customers' documents to include a portal link; do not invite customers who must not see one.

sources.quote: If your customer has been invited to the Billing Portal, they receive a link to manage their subscription (the “Management URL”) automatically at the bottom of their statements, invoices, and receipts.

condition: A Management URL is issued for a customer.

provider_outcome.effect: The URL changes periodically for security and is valid for only 65 days.

app_must: Store the URL with its expires_at and fetch a new one before it expires rather than keeping it indefinitely.

sources.quote: **This link changes periodically for security and is only valid for 65 days.**
Management URLs are good for 65 days, so you should re-use a previously generated one as much as possible.

condition: Enable Webhooks is called with webhooks_enabled.

provider_outcome.effect: Webhook sending is switched on (or off) for the whole site, not for one endpoint.

app_must: Remember that this switch is site-wide and affects every configured endpoint.

sources.quote: Enables webhooks for your site.
You can enable or disable webhooks as needed.

condition: Any API request is made.
app_must: Authenticate every request with HTTP Basic over HTTPS, using the site API key as the username and x as the password.

sources.quote: The `username` is a Maxio Chargify API key. The `password` is `x`.
API Authentication is implemented as HTTP Basic Authentication over TLS (HTTPS).

condition: An individual statement or invoice is fetched with Accept application/pdf or a .pdf extension.

provider_outcome.effect: The document is returned as a PDF.

app_must: Use application/pdf or .pdf only on GETs for individual statements and invoices.

sources.quote: GETs for individual statements and invoices may also be requested as PDF using `application/pdf` or appending `.pdf` to the resource URI.

condition: A boolean field in a response is null.

provider_outcome.effect: null may mean false, but not in every case; it can also mean no data is available.

app_must: Do not map null booleans to false blindly; treat null as unknown unless the field's meaning says otherwise.

sources.quote: For boolean fields, note that a value of `null` may be considered as false. However, this is not true across all cases.

condition: A response contains timestamp fields.

provider_outcome.effect: Timestamps are in the site's time zone, ISO 8601 with a UTC offset and no fractional seconds.

app_must: Parse timestamps with their offset and do not assume UTC.

sources.quote: Timestamp fields in API responses (e.g. `created_at`, `next_assessment_at`) are returned in the timezone of the Advanced Billing site, formatted as ISO 8601 with a UTC offset and no fractional seconds

condition: A response contains date-only fields (for example issue_date, due_date, paid_date).

provider_outcome.effect: They are YYYY-MM-DD strings giving the site's local calendar date, not the UTC date.

app_must: Treat date-only fields as site-local dates without converting them through UTC.

sources.quote: These are plain `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, and the date itself reflects the site's local calendar date rather than UTC.

condition: A request sends a date without a time.

provider_outcome.effect: The API uses noon in the site's time zone.

app_must: Send a full timestamp with offset when a time other than noon in the site's time zone is meant.

sources.quote: If only a date is provided, the API defaults to noon in the site's time zone.

condition: A request sends a date and time without a time zone offset.

provider_outcome.effect: The time of day is taken in the site's time zone.

app_must: Add a UTC offset to request timestamps unless site-local time is intended.

sources.quote: If a date and time are provided, the API uses that time of day in the site's time zone.

condition: A request sends a date, time and time zone offset.

provider_outcome.effect: The API uses that absolute instant and shows it back in the site's time zone.

app_must: Compare returned timestamps as instants, since they come back in the site's time zone rather than the zone you sent.

sources.quote: If a date, time, and timezone offset are provided, the API uses that absolute instant and displays it in the site's time zone.

condition: A response contains decimal numbers.

provider_outcome.effect: Decimal numbers are serialized as strings to avoid losing precision.

app_must: Parse decimal strings with a decimal library, not floating point.

sources.quote: In order to prevent losing precision, we serialize decimal numbers as strings instead of as JSON numbers.

condition: A response contains amount fields.

provider_outcome.effect: Top-level totals (such as total_amount, tax_amount) are rounded to the currency's smallest unit, but line-item unit_price and quantity can carry more decimal places.

app_must: Do your own rounding where needed and do not assume every amount is rounded to the currency's minor unit.

sources.quote: Not all amount fields are rounded to the currency's smallest denomination. Top-level totals (e.g., `total_amount`, `tax_amount`) are rounded to the smallest denomination of the currency.
It is up to API consumers to parse the string into a decimal number representation and do any rounding necessary for your application.

condition: A resource (such as an invoice or credit note) exposes both a numeric id and a string uid.

provider_outcome.effect: The uid is a separate opaque identifier and is not interchangeable with the numeric id.

app_must: Use id or uid exactly where each is asked for and never substitute one for the other.

sources.quote: This is distinct from the numeric `id` and should not be used interchangeably with it.

condition: A request is authenticated with the username and password used to log in to the web interface.
app_must: Obtain API credentials (API keys) separately and never use web login credentials for API calls.

sources.quote: Your API login credentials are not the same as the credentials you use to log in to the web interface. You must obtain your API credentials separately

condition: Maxio adds endpoints, response attributes, optional parameters or export fields.

provider_outcome.effect: Such backwards-compatible changes are made without advance notice.

app_must: Ignore unknown response attributes and export fields instead of failing on them.

sources.quote: We consider the following changes to be backwards compatible and may make them without advance notice:
Adding new API endpoints, or adding new attributes in the responses of existing endpoints

condition: An ID attribute is stored or parsed by the client.

provider_outcome.effect: The type or length of ID attributes may change without notice; most are integers today.

app_must: Store IDs in a type that does not assume a fixed integer size or type.

sources.quote: Changing the type or length of any of the ID attributes
For example, most IDs are currently integers, but you should not assume that this will always be the case.

condition: A client reads attributes from an API response.

provider_outcome.effect: The order of attributes in a response may change.

app_must: Read response attributes by name, never by position.

sources.quote: In addition, you should not depend on the order of attributes within the API response as this may change.

condition: A list endpoint that uses the standard per_page parameter is called without per_page or with per_page above 200.

provider_outcome.effect: Usually 20 items are returned by default; a per_page above 200 is changed to 200.

app_must: Page through lists with page and per_page (at most 200) instead of expecting everything in one response.

sources.quote: When an endpoint returns a list of items, it will be paginated. Usually, 20 items will be returned by default, and you may request up to a maximum of 200 at a time.
Default value is 20. The maximum allowed values is 200; any per_page value over 200 will be changed to 200.

condition: A list endpoint is asked for a page beyond the last page of results.

provider_outcome.effect: An empty result set is returned rather than an error.

app_must: Stop paging when a page comes back empty.

sources.quote: If there are no results to return, then an empty result set will be returned.

condition: A list request sends a date_field value other than created_at or updated_at.

provider_outcome.effect: The value is ignored and the date filters are not applied, so unfiltered records are returned.

app_must: Send only date_field values the endpoint supports and check that results are actually filtered.

sources.quote: Now if other values as `created_at` or `updated_at` are passed in `date_field`, we just ignore them, and filters are not applied.

condition: More than 4 API calls run at the same time for one subdomain.

provider_outcome.effect: Calls above the 4-call concurrency limit may be queued until concurrency drops.

app_must: Limit the integration to 4 concurrent requests per subdomain.

sources.quote: we handle call limiting based on concurrency, and a maximum of 4 concurrent API calls can be made.
Any concurrency that goes above 4 is at risk for being queued for processing after the concurrency once again drops to acceptable ranges.

condition: A large synchronization or burst of requests trips the rate-based failsafe.

provider_outcome.effect: Requests are slowed and throttled instead of being rejected at once.

app_must: When responses slow down, do not add parallel requests; reduce concurrency.

sources.quote: Advanced Billing will slow and throttle requests.
If you see your responses coming in slower, do not parallelize your requests or try to make more concurrent requests to speed things up.

condition: Too many requests are slowed or the account queue is full of concurrent requests.

provider_outcome.error: Your request was denied due to a usage violation. You can track this request with support by referencing …

app_must: On 429, pause requests for a few minutes and then continue more slowly or with less concurrency.

sources.quote: you’ll likely receive an HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` response code with a message and a reference code:
your code should be prepared to handle it by pausing its queries, waiting a few minutes, and then proceeding slower (or with less concurrency).

condition: Low-priority requests (reports and exports) arrive while the system is balancing load.

provider_outcome.effect: Critical endpoints such as new signups and component allocations are favoured, and reports and exports are slowed down.

app_must: Expect report and export calls to be slower under load and schedule them away from critical traffic.

sources.quote: By dynamically balancing, we can slow down "low priority" requests (reports and exports), while still handling large unexpected surges in signups.

condition: A client connects with TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1.

provider_outcome.effect: Clients that do not support TLS 1.2 no longer work.

app_must: Connect with TLS 1.2 or newer.

sources.quote: you must connect to the API via TLS 1.2 (or better).
Advanced Billing no longer supports TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 over HTTPS on the chargify.com domain. Any older browsers or API clients that do not support TLS 1.2 will no longer work.

condition: Many simultaneous requests go to the same endpoint, or to an expensive endpoint.

provider_outcome.effect: Expensive endpoints have lower limits, and simultaneous requests to the same endpoint are queued behind each other.

app_must: Spread requests over time instead of sending many at once to the same endpoint.

sources.quote: Expensive endpoints have lower limits than fast endpoints.
When you do that, your requests will be "queued" behind yourself. One request must wait for the one in front of it to finish.

condition: A request (including the time spent at the payment gateway) is not processed within 120 seconds.

provider_outcome.effect: The request times out.

app_must: Allow for the 120-second cut-off, and after a timeout check the gateway status and retry safely with a uniqueness_token.

sources.quote: Advanced Billing imposes a cut-off time of 120 seconds for all requests to all endpoints.
If a request is not processed by the combination of Advanced Billing and your gateway within the 120 second guideline, the request will time out.

condition: The merchant's Advanced Billing subscription is canceled.

provider_outcome.error: Your Advanced Billing account has been canceled. Please contact support@maxio.com to reactivate.

app_must: Treat this 422 as an account block, not a request validation error, and contact Maxio support.

sources.quote: Your Advanced Billing subscription is canceled.
Your Advanced Billing account has been canceled. Please contact support@maxio.com to reactivate.

condition: The merchant's Advanced Billing trial has ended.

provider_outcome.error: Your trial has ended, please contact sales.

app_must: Treat this 422 as an account block and contact Maxio sales.

sources.quote: Your Advanced Billing trial has reached an end.
Your trial has ended, please contact sales.

condition: The site being called is in the process of clearing site data (requests to other sites in a good state are not blocked).

provider_outcome.error: Site data clearing is in progress. Please try later.

app_must: Wait until site data clearing finishes before calling that site again.

sources.quote: The site you're making a request for is in the process of ["clearing site data"]
Site data clearing is in progress. Please try later.

condition: The site being called has been deleted.

provider_outcome.error: This site has been deleted.

app_must: Stop calling a deleted site and point the integration at a live site.

sources.quote: The site you're making a request for has been deleted.
This site has been deleted.

condition: A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE request carries a top-level uniqueness_token already used by an earlier request.

provider_outcome.error: DuplicatePrevention::DuplicateSubmissionError

app_must: Send a long random uniqueness_token (such as a UUID) at the top level of every data-changing request you may retry.

sources.quote: To prevent these duplicates, Advanced Billing accepts a `uniqueness_token` parameter on any request that changes data: `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE`. Send the token at the top level of the request body, alongside the resource object rather than nested inside the object.
If a second request arrives with the same `uniqueness_token`, the second request is rejected with a `409 Conflict` response code and a duplicate submission error.
If a second request arrives with the same token, the second request is rejected with a `409 Conflict` and a duplicate submission error instead of being processed again.

app_must: Use component_id, not product_id, to tell component charges from product charges.

sources.quote: This may be set even for component charges, so true product-only (non-component) charges will also have a nil `component_id`.

condition: A consolidated (parent) invoice is returned.

provider_outcome.effect: The parent invoice has no line items of its own; its totals aggregate the segments.

app_must: Read a consolidated invoice's lines from its segments, not from the parent.

sources.quote: "Parent" invoices do not have lines of their own, but they have subtotals and totals which aggregate the member invoice segments.

condition: Branding Themes are not enabled for the site.

provider_outcome.effect: branding_theme_id is not available on invoices.

app_must: Treat branding_theme_id as optional and only rely on it when Branding Themes are enabled.

sources.quote: Available only when Branding Themes are enabled for the site.

condition: An invoice is returned.

provider_outcome.effect: total_amount is computed as subtotal_amount - discount_amount + tax_amount.

app_must: Use the returned total_amount rather than recomputing it from line items.

sources.quote: The invoice total, which is `subtotal_amount - discount_amount + tax_amount`.

condition: An invoice is returned.

provider_outcome.effect: due_amount is computed as total_amount - credit_amount - paid_amount.

app_must: Use due_amount as the amount still owed; it already nets out credits and payments.

sources.quote: Amount due on the invoice, which is `total_amount - credit_amount - paid_amount`.

condition: An invoice has received only partial payment.

provider_outcome.effect: paid_date stays empty until the invoice is paid in full.

app_must: Do not treat an empty paid_date as no payment; check paid_amount for partial payments.

sources.quote: If partial payments are applied to the invoice, this date will not be present until payment has been made in full.

condition: An invoice or credit note returns issue_date, due_date or paid_date.

provider_outcome.effect: The date is the site's local calendar date, not a UTC date.

app_must: Interpret invoice and credit-note dates in the site's time zone.

sources.quote: These are plain `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, and the date itself reflects the site's local calendar date rather than UTC.

condition: Line-item amounts are summed or recomputed by the client.

provider_outcome.effect: subtotal_amount is the canonical line amount; the sum of line total_amounts may not equal the invoice total_amount because of rounding.

app_must: Reconcile against the invoice totals, not the sum of line total_amount values.

sources.quote: This is the canonical amount of record for the line - when rounding differences are in play, `subtotal_amount` takes precedence over the value derived from `quantity * unit_price`
Therefore, due to rounding or precision errors, the sum of line `total_amount`s may not equal the invoice `total_amount`.

condition: A line item shows discount_amount or tax_amount.

provider_outcome.effect: The per-line discount and tax are approximations of the invoice-level amounts apportioned across lines.

app_must: Use the invoice-level discount_amount and tax_amount for accounting, not the sum of per-line values.

sources.quote: The value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total discount among many lines.
The value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total tax among many lines.

condition: A line item is returned with tax_included.

provider_outcome.effect: tax_included is inherited from the source price point; custom or ad hoc lines always return false.

app_must: Do not expect tax-inclusive pricing on custom ad hoc lines.

sources.quote: The value is inherited from the source price point's `tax_included` setting. Custom or ad-hoc line items (which have no associated price point) always return `false`.

condition: A line item was priced with a tiered scheme.

provider_outcome.effect: unit_price is the blended average per unit and tiered_unit_price is true.

app_must: Do not multiply unit_price by quantity to re-derive tiered charges; use subtotal_amount.

sources.quote: When tiered pricing was used (i.e., not every unit was actually priced at the same price) this will be the blended average cost per unit and the `tiered_unit_price` field will be set to `true`.

condition: at_time is omitted.

provider_outcome.effect: MRR is returned for the current time; with at_time it is returned for that historic time.

app_must: Send at_time in ISO 8601 when you need MRR at a past moment.

sources.quote: Returns your site's current MRR, including plan and usage breakouts.
submit a timestamp in ISO8601 format to request MRR for a historic time.

condition: An offer is returned from a site without Multifrequency enabled.

provider_outcome.effect: The offer items' interval and interval_unit properties are only available on sites with Multifrequency enabled.

app_must: Treat offer item interval and interval_unit as optional and absent unless the site has Multifrequency.

sources.quote: an interval of '30' coupled with an interval_unit of day would mean this component price point would renew every 30 days. This property is only available for sites with Multifrequency enabled.
A string representing the interval unit for this component price point, either month or day. This property is only available for sites with Multifrequency enabled.

condition: The chargify_token in the path does not match an Advanced Billing token, which can only be obtained through Chargify.js.

provider_outcome.error: Advanced Billing token not found

app_must: Obtain the token through Chargify.js before reading it, and treat a 404 as an unknown token.

sources.quote: - Advanced Billing token not found
To obtain a One Time Token you have to use [Chargify.js]

condition: A one-time token is used for ACH (bank account) data on a gateway other than Authorize.Net or Stripe.

provider_outcome.effect: One-time tokens hold ACH data only for Authorize.Net or Stripe.

app_must: Use one-time tokens for ACH only on Authorize.Net or Stripe sites.

sources.quote: One Time Tokens aka Advanced Billing Tokens house the credit card or ACH (Authorize.Net or Stripe only) data for a customer.

condition: A product family is returned on a site where surcharging is not enabled.

provider_outcome.effect: The surcharging field is left out of the product family.

app_must: Treat a missing surcharging field as normal on sites without surcharging.

sources.quote: Whether surcharging applies to this product family. Only included on sites where surcharging is enabled.

condition: The product family is given in the path as handle:<handle> instead of a numeric id.

provider_outcome.effect: The product family is looked up by handle.

app_must: Use either the numeric id or handle:<handle> in the path.

sources.quote: The product family can be specified either with the id number, or with the `handle:my-family` format.

conflict: The path parameter schema types id as an integer, while the operation description accepts the handle:my-family format; the record follows the description.

condition: The site has Relationship Invoicing enabled.

provider_outcome.effect: The response carries extra properties (customer_hierarchy_enabled, whopays_enabled, whopays_default_payer); multi_frequency_enabled is present only when relationship invoicing is active.

app_must: Treat the relationship-invoicing properties of the site as optional and expect them to be absent on other sites.

sources.quote: If the site has Relationship invoicing enabled, additional properties are returned in the response:
Whether the site has the multi-frequency billing feature enabled. Only present when relationship invoicing is active.

condition: Site stats are requested in XML.
app_must: Request site stats as JSON.

sources.quote: This API call only answers with JSON responses. An XML version is not provided.

condition: current_billing_amount_in_cents is wanted from an operation other than readSubscription.

provider_outcome.effect: The field (balance plus estimated renewal amount) is returned only by readSubscription, as it is compute intensive.

app_must: Read the single subscription to get current_billing_amount_in_cents.

sources.quote: The balance in cents plus the estimated renewal amount in cents. Returned ONLY for the readSubscription operation as it's a compute intensive operation.

conflict: Subscription-List-Include.yaml offers current_billing_amount as a listSubscriptions include; the record follows Subscription.yaml.

condition: Referrals are enabled for the site.

provider_outcome.effect: Every subscription response includes a referral_code.

app_must: Read referral_code only on sites with referrals enabled and treat it as absent otherwise.

sources.quote: When referrals are enabled, every subscription includes a `referral_code` in the subscription API response.

condition: Coupon details are wanted on a subscription.

provider_outcome.effect: The coupons array is returned only by Read Subscription and only with include[]=coupons.

app_must: Call readSubscription with include[]=coupons to get coupon data.

sources.quote: Additional coupon data. To use this data you also have to include the following param in the request: `include[]=coupons`. Only in Read Subscription Endpoint.

conflict: Subscription-List-Include.yaml also lists coupons as a listSubscriptions include; the record follows Subscription.yaml.

condition: Referrals are enabled on the site.

provider_outcome.effect: Every subscription response includes a referral_code the customer can share.

app_must: Read referral_code from the subscription when referrals are enabled.

sources.quote: When referrals are enabled, every subscription includes a `referral_code` in the subscription API response.

condition: component_id in the path is a component handle rather than the numeric id.
app_must: Prefix a component handle with handle: in the path; otherwise send the numeric id.

sources.quote: The Advanced Billing id of the component. Alternatively, the component's handle prefixed by `handle:`
Either the Advanced Billing id for the component or the component's handle prefixed by `handle:`

conflict: readSubscriptionComponent declares component_id as an integer while its description allows a handle: string; this record follows the description.

condition: Several products/components grant the same feature, or a usage_limit feature is granted with different periodicities.

provider_outcome.effect: Entitlements are collapsed into one entry per feature key and periodicity window; different periodicities come back as separate entries sharing one feature_key.

app_must: Key entitlements by periodicity_key, not by feature_key.

sources.quote: Returns every feature a subscription is entitled to, collapsed into one entry per feature key and periodicity window across all products and components on the subscription.
Entries are aggregated per feature key and periodicity window, not per feature key alone.
That endpoint collapses every product and component on the subscription into one entry per feature key and periodicity window.

condition: An aggregated entitlement has a periodicity window.

provider_outcome.effect: periodicity_key is the prefixed feature key suffixed with :{interval}:{unit}; it equals feature_key when periodicity is null.

app_must: Use periodicity_key as the unique id of an entry.

sources.quote: Uniquely identifies this aggregated entry: the prefixed feature key, suffixed with `:{interval}:{unit}` when the entitlement has a periodicity window. Equal to `feature_key` when `periodicity` is `null`.

condition: Several products or components on a subscription grant the same feature.

provider_outcome.effect: Entitlements are collapsed into one entry per feature key and periodicity window, so different periodicities give separate entries with their own periodicity_key.

app_must: Key entitlements by periodicity_key, not only by feature_key.

sources.quote: That endpoint collapses every product and component on the subscription into one entry per feature key and periodicity window.

condition: The subscription is not in a live state (active, trialing, assessing, past_due or soft_failure).

provider_outcome.effect: enabled is false regardless of the aggregated value; entitlements stay enabled while the subscription is in dunning.

app_must: Check enabled before granting access in your application.

sources.quote: The field is `false` whenever the subscription isn't in a live state (`active`, `trialing`, `assessing`, `past_due`, or `soft_failure`), regardless of the value. Note that entitlements stay enabled while a subscription is in dunning.

`enabled` reflects both the aggregated value and the subscription's state. The field is `false` whenever the subscription is not in a live state (`active`, `trialing`, `assessing`, `past_due`, `soft_failure`), regardless of the aggregated value.

condition: More than one contributor grants the same access_right feature key and periodicity.

provider_outcome.effect: Values are combined with boolean OR: true if any contributor grants access; source_products lists only contributors that granted true.

app_must: Treat an access_right as granted when any product or component grants it.

sources.quote: features are combined with a boolean OR. If any contributor grants access, the aggregate is `true`. `source_products` only lists the contributors that granted `true`.

condition: More than one contributor grants the same usage_limit feature key.

provider_outcome.effect: Values are summed across contributors sharing the same periodicity window; grants with different periodicities are not summed and are returned as separate entries.

app_must: Read the summed limit per periodicity_key; do not add entries of different periodicities yourself.

sources.quote: features are summed across every contributor sharing the same periodicity window. `source_products` lists every contributor. Grants with different periodicities are not summed together.

condition: More than one contributor grants the same service_right feature key.

provider_outcome.effect: Values are not combined; one contributor's value wins, and which one is not defined.

app_must: Avoid granting the same service_right key from several products/components, or do not depend on which value is returned.

sources.quote: features are not combined: one contributor's value wins. Do not rely on which one when several grant the same feature key.

condition: The subscription is not in a live state (active, trialing, assessing, past_due, soft_failure), e.g. awaiting_signup, canceled, expired or on hold.

provider_outcome.effect: enabled is false for every entitlement, regardless of the aggregated value.

app_must: Check enabled, not value, before granting access in your application.

sources.quote: The field is `false` whenever the subscription is not in a live state (`active`, `trialing`, `assessing`, `past_due`, `soft_failure`), regardless of the aggregated value.
`false` otherwise, including for `awaiting_signup`, canceled, expired, and on-hold subscriptions.
Most integrations should check `enabled` before granting access in their own application.

condition: The subscription is in dunning (past_due or soft_failure).

provider_outcome.effect: Entitlements stay enabled through dunning.

app_must: Do not expect entitlements to switch off while the subscription is in dunning; restrict access yourself if your policy requires it.

sources.quote: Entitlements deliberately stay enabled through dunning.
Note that entitlements stay enabled while a subscription is in dunning.

condition: The aggregated value is not truthy for the feature's kind (for example false or 0).

provider_outcome.effect: enabled is false even when the subscription is live.

app_must: Check enabled rather than the presence of an entry.

sources.quote: `true` only when the aggregated value is truthy for this feature's kind, and the subscription is in a live state

condition: An aggregated entitlement is returned.

provider_outcome.effect: value is coerced by type: boolean for access_right (and boolean service_right), number for usage_limit (and numeric service_right), string for text service_right.

app_must: Parse value according to type rather than as the string stored on the feature catalog item.

sources.quote: The aggregated value, coerced according to `type`: a boolean for `access_right` (and boolean `service_right`), a number for `usage_limit` (and numeric `service_right`), or a string for text `service_right`.

condition: An aggregated entitlement is returned.

provider_outcome.effect: feature_key is the template key prefixed by kind: feature.* for access_right, usage.* for usage_limit, service.* for service_right.

app_must: Match entitlements on the prefixed key (e.g. feature.sso), not the bare template key.

sources.quote: The feature's key, prefixed by kind: `feature.*` for `access_right`, `usage.*` for `usage_limit`, `service.*` for `service_right`.

condition: readSubscriptionGroup is called without include[]=current_billing_amount_in_cents.

provider_outcome.effect: current_billing_amount_in_cents is left out of the response.

app_must: Pass include[]=current_billing_amount_in_cents when the group's billing amount is needed.

sources.quote: Current billing amount for the subscription group is not returned by default. If this information is desired, the `include[]=current_billing_amount_in_cents` parameter must be provided with the request.

condition: A wallet's grants are returned.

provider_outcome.effect: Every grant, including spent and expired ones, is listed in drain order: soonest-expiring first, evergreen grants last.

app_must: Filter spent or expired grants yourself; do not assume the array holds only open grants.

sources.quote: Every grant on the wallet, including ones already spent or expired, in drain order (the order debits would consume the still-open ones in): the soonest-expiring grant first, evergreen grants last.
Spent and expired grants stay in the array too; nothing is filtered out of it.

condition: A wallet paired with a meter is returned.

provider_outcome.effect: Only Read Wallet computes a live balance, and only for an active wallet on a site with metered consumption enabled; every other response reports the stored balance (balance equal to posted_balance) with the metered_* fields null.

app_must: Call Read Wallet when you need the live metered balance and reconcile against posted_balance.

sources.quote: but only [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet) actually computes a live balance from it, and only for an active wallet on a site with metered consumption enabled.

reports the stored balance as of the last ledger write (`balance` equal to `posted_balance`, and `remaining` equal to `posted_remaining`) and leaves the three `metered_*` fields `null`, even for a metered wallet.

condition: Live metered usage cannot be read fresh when a metered wallet is read.

provider_outcome.effect: metered_stale is true and balance falls back to the last known snapshot, while posted_balance stays exact.

app_must: Check metered_stale and wait metered_recheck_after_seconds before reading again.

sources.quote: `metered_stale` is `true` if live usage couldn't be read fresh (in which case `balance` falls back to the last known snapshot, and `posted_balance` stays exact)

condition: A wallet's grants are returned.

provider_outcome.effect: Grants are listed in drain order (soonest-expiring first, evergreen grants last) and spent or expired grants stay in the array.

app_must: Filter spent and expired grants yourself when you only need open ones.

sources.quote: Grants are listed in drain order: the order debits would consume the still-open ones in, with the soonest-expiring grant first and evergreen grants (`expires_at: null`) last. Spent and expired grants stay in the array too; nothing is filtered out of it.

condition: A wallet response carries a depletion_policy the app does not know.

provider_outcome.effect: New depletion_policy values are expected over time; hard_stop is the only one today.

app_must: Treat depletion_policy as an open string and do not fail on unknown values.

sources.quote: More values are expected over time, so treat this as an open string and don't fail on one you don't recognize.

condition: readWallet is called for an active, metered wallet on a site with metered consumption enabled.

provider_outcome.effect: balance and grants' remaining include usage not yet posted to the ledger (through metered_through_at), so balance can be below posted_balance; this is the only operation that computes it.

app_must: Enforce against balance from readWallet, and reconcile the ledger against posted_balance.

sources.quote: For an active, metered wallet on a site with metered consumption enabled, this is the only operation that computes a live balance from meter usage
only [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet) actually computes a live balance from it, and only for an active wallet on a site with metered consumption enabled.

condition: readWallet cannot read a metered wallet's live usage fresh.

provider_outcome.effect: metered_stale is true and balance falls back to the last known snapshot, while posted_balance stays exact.

app_must: Check metered_stale before trusting balance as live.

sources.quote: `true` when live usage could not be read fresh and `balance` reflects an earlier snapshot.
`metered_stale` is `true` if live usage couldn't be read fresh (in which case `balance` falls back to the last known snapshot, and `posted_balance` stays exact)

condition: readWallet returns a live metered balance.

provider_outcome.effect: metered_recheck_after_seconds says how long to wait before reading again to see usage past metered_through_at.

sources.quote: How many seconds to wait before re-reading `balance` to see usage past `metered_through_at`.
`metered_recheck_after_seconds` suggests how long to wait before reading again.

condition: readWallet is called for an archived metered wallet.

condition: Events are streamed for a subscription whose event-based component is not activated.

condition: An event payload includes chargify.id.
