Set to an empty string to cancel a delayed product change.

condition: A delayed product change is scheduled.

provider_outcome.effect: A subscription_product_change_scheduled webhook fires as soon as the change is scheduled.

app_must: Use subscription_product_change_scheduled to react before the renewal.

sources.quote: A delayed product change has been successfully scheduled for a subscription

condition: A subscription's product (or product version) changes successfully.

provider_outcome.effect: A subscription_product_change webhook is sent.

app_must: Handle subscription_product_change for product changes, migrations and version changes.

sources.quote: A successful change from an old product to a new product for a subscription. This webhook will fire for a product version change.

condition: updateSubscriptionGroupMembers is sent with a member_ids array that leaves out current members (an empty array leaves out all of them).

provider_outcome.effect: Every current member missing from member_ids is removed from the group.

app_must: Send the full intended member list, including members already in the group.

sources.quote: should contain an array of both subscription IDs to set as group members and subscription IDs already present in the groups. Not including them will result in removing them from the subscription group. To clean up members, just leave the array empty.

condition: updateWallet is sent with attributes other than name (wallet product, meter, conversion rate, price point and so on).

provider_outcome.effect: Every attribute other than name is ignored; those are fixed for the life of the wallet.

app_must: Create a new wallet when anything other than the name must change.

sources.quote: Only `name` is editable; any other attribute in the body is ignored.
After creation, only the wallet's `name` can be changed, with [Update Wallet]($e/Wallets/updateWallet). Everything else is fixed for the life of the wallet.
the Wallet Product behind a wallet cannot be changed after the wallet is created.

condition: Anything other than a wallet's name would be changed after creation, including its Wallet Product.
app_must: Set the Wallet Product and settings correctly at creation; change only name with Update Wallet.

sources.quote: After creation, only the wallet's `name` can be changed, with [Update Wallet]($e/Wallets/updateWallet). Everything else is fixed for the life of the wallet.
the Wallet Product behind a wallet cannot be changed after the wallet is created.

condition: updateWallet is sent with no editable attribute in the body.

provider_outcome.effect: code parameter_missing

app_must: Include name in every updateWallet body.

sources.quote: Includes a body with no editable attribute (`parameter_missing`)

condition: updateWalletProduct is sent with unit_name, handle, price_point or price_points.

provider_outcome.effect: Those fields are silently ignored and nothing about them changes.

app_must: Change only name, description, taxable, tax_code, accounting_code and item_category on update.

sources.quote: `unit_name`, `handle`, `price_point`, and `price_points` are not accepted here: the request still returns `200`, but those fields are silently ignored and nothing about them changes.
the unit name, handle, and price points are fixed once created.

condition: updateWalletProduct leaves some mutable fields out of the body.

provider_outcome.effect: Omitted fields keep their current values.

app_must: Send only the fields you want to change.

sources.quote: Updates the Wallet Product's catalog-facing fields. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

condition: The coupon code being validated is not found.

provider_outcome.error: Coupon code could not be found.

app_must: Show the customer an invalid-code message on 404 rather than treating it as a failure of the service.

sources.quote: errors: Coupon code could not be found.

condition: The referral code is not valid or not applicable within the site.

provider_outcome.error: Referral code is invalid.

app_must: Treat 404 as an invalid code and do not pass it as ref when creating the subscription.

sources.quote: Referral code is invalid.
A valid referral code returns `200 OK`. An invalid referral code returns `404 NOT FOUND`.

condition: A bank account is verified on a site whose gateway is not Stripe.
app_must: Call bank account verification only for bank accounts stored with Stripe.

sources.quote: Verifies a bank account. Submit the two small deposit amounts the customer received in their bank account to verify the bank account. (Stripe only)

condition: Verification has already been attempted 10 times for the bank account.

provider_outcome.error: You have tried to verify this bank account 10 times. To continue trying to verify the account, please reach out to us directly.
provider_outcome.effect: Further verification attempts are refused until support is contacted.

app_must: Limit deposit-amount attempts and route the customer to support after the tenth failure.

sources.quote: You have tried to verify this bank account 10 times. To continue trying to verify the account, please reach out to us directly.

condition: Verification is submitted before the customer has received the two small deposits, or with amounts that are not the deposits received.
app_must: Wait until the customer sees the two deposits in the bank account and submit exactly those amounts in cents.

sources.quote: Submit the two small deposit amounts the customer received in their bank account to verify the bank account.

condition: The two deposit amounts are provided successfully for a bank account.

provider_outcome.effect: The bank account's verified flag records that it has been verified.

app_must: Read verified on the bank account profile to know whether verification has completed.

sources.quote: Denotes whether a bank account has been verified by providing the amounts of two small deposits made into the account.

condition: The subscription's advance invoice is not in open status when a void is requested.
app_must: Void an advance invoice only while its status is open.

sources.quote: A `reason` is required to void, and the invoice must have an open status.

condition: An advance invoice is voided.

provider_outcome.effect: Prepayments and credits that were applied to the invoice are returned to the subscription.

app_must: Expect the subscription's prepayment and service credit balances to rise again after voiding an advance invoice.

sources.quote: Voiding causes any prepayments and credits that were applied to the invoice to be returned to the subscription.

condition: The subscription's advance invoice for the period has been voided.

provider_outcome.effect: A new advance invoice can be issued for the same period.

app_must: Allow issuing a new advance invoice after voiding the old one.

sources.quote: Voids a subscription's existing advance invoice. Once voided, it can later be regenerated if desired.

condition: An invoice whose status is not open, canceled or pending is voided.

provider_outcome.error: Invoice status must be 'open', 'canceled', or 'pending' and non-consolidated to be voided.

app_must: Void only open, canceled or pending invoices.

sources.quote: Voids any invoice with the "open" or "canceled" status.
Invoice status must be 'open', 'canceled', or 'pending' and non-consolidated to be voided.

condition: A pending invoice that is a consolidated invoice is voided.

provider_outcome.error: Invoice status must be 'open', 'canceled', or 'pending' and non-consolidated to be voided.

app_must: Do not void pending consolidated invoices.

sources.quote: It will also allow voiding of an invoice with the "pending" status if it is not a consolidated invoice.

conflict: The error message reads as if every consolidated invoice is refused, while the description limits the restriction to pending invoices; the record follows the description.

condition: A proforma invoice that is not in draft status is voided.

provider_outcome.error: Only draft proforma invoices may be voided.

app_must: Void only draft proforma invoices.

sources.quote: Voids a proforma invoice that has the status "draft".
Only draft proforma invoices may be voided.
If the invoice identified by {uid} does not have the appropriate status, the response will have HTTP status code 422 and an error message.

condition: A product that has a handle is archived.

provider_outcome.effect: The archived product comes back with handle null and archived_at set.

app_must: Keep product ids; do not look an archived product up by its old handle.

condition: Two identical cancel requests for the same active subscription are sent at the same moment.

provider_outcome.effect: Both return 200 with the same canceled subscription (one canceled_at); neither gets 'The subscription is already canceled', which a cancel sent after the first does get.

app_must: Do not rely on the 'already canceled' 422 to detect a duplicate cancel; read the state.

condition: A subscription with an unpaid balance is canceled immediately (no schedule parameters).

provider_outcome.effect: balance_in_cents stays as it was (1000) and current_period_ends_at and next_assessment_at keep the old renewal date; nothing is credited or cleared.

app_must: Do not show next_assessment_at as a coming bill on a canceled subscription, and keep collecting balance_in_cents after cancellation.

condition: An on_hold subscription is canceled.

provider_outcome.effect: It is canceled with previous_state on_hold; the cancel response still shows on_hold_at, but a read right after shows on_hold_at null.

app_must: Read the subscription after canceling a held one instead of trusting on_hold_at in the cancel response.

condition: A write is refused with 422.

provider_outcome.error: {"error": "The subscription is already canceled"} / {"errors": {"usage": "can't be blank"}} / {"errors": {"currency": ["Currency must be defined on the site level.", ...]}} / {"errors": ["Reference: must be unique - that value has been taken."]}
provider_outcome.effect: The error body has three shapes: a single error string (cancel of a canceled subscription), errors keyed by field with a string or a list (usage, currency prices), or a plain errors list (most others).

app_must: Parse 422 bodies for error, errors as a list, and errors as an object of fields before showing a message.

condition: A customer is created with a reference another customer already has, including a second identical create sent right after or at the same moment.

provider_outcome.error: Reference: must be unique - that value has been taken.
provider_outcome.effect: Of two identical creates sent at the same moment, one returned 201 and the other this 422; no second customer was made.

app_must: Send a reference on every create and treat this 422 as 'already created': look the customer up by reference.

condition: A customer is created without organization.

provider_outcome.effect: organization is null in the create response and in a read right after; it is not filled from the first and last name.

app_must: Do not expect organization to be filled for you; send it, or show the person's name yourself.
conflict: maxio-c4:createCustomer.12: the docs say an omitted organization is filled with the first and last name; the sandbox left it null on create and on the read after; this record follows the sandbox.

condition: A product is created with a handle another product on the site already has, including the same create sent again right after.

provider_outcome.error: API Handle: must be unique - '<handle>' has been taken by another Product in this Site.
provider_outcome.effect: No second product is created.

app_must: Use the handle as the product's key: treat this 422 on a retry as 'already created' and read the product by handle.

condition: Two identical createProduct requests with the same handle are sent at the same moment.

provider_outcome.effect: One returns 201; the other returns 500 with an empty body instead of the duplicate-handle 422.

app_must: After a 500 from createProduct, look the product up by handle before retrying.

condition: price_in_cents is negative (-1).

provider_outcome.error: Currency prices: is invalid. / Price: must be greater than or equal to 0.
provider_outcome.effect: A price of 0 is accepted; -1 is refused with a currency-prices message as well, though no currency prices were sent.

app_must: Check prices are 0 or more before creating a product, and show the price message rather than the currency-prices one.

condition: A product is created with only name, description, price and interval (no handle and no card settings).

provider_outcome.effect: handle is null (none is generated), request_credit_card and require_credit_card are true even for a $0 price, trial_type is payment_expected, and a default price point named Original with a uuid: handle is created.

app_must: Send a handle and the card settings you want on every new product; do not rely on the defaults.

condition: A new product is created.

provider_outcome.effect: public_signup_pages is [] in the create response (and still [] when the product is archived later): no signup page is shown for it.

app_must: Do not expect a Public Signup Page for a product created through the API; create or link one yourself if you need it.
conflict: maxio-c4:createProduct.102: the docs say a Public Signup Page is created automatically for a new product; the sandbox's responses list public_signup_pages as []; this record follows the sandbox.

condition: A currency price is sent for EUR, which is not defined in this site's currency settings.

provider_outcome.error: Currency must be defined on the site level.
provider_outcome.effect: The message comes back three times under errors.currency; repeated and concurrent calls get the same refusal and no currency price is stored.

app_must: Offer only currencies the site defines, and fix the site's currency settings rather than retrying.

condition: A currency price is negative (-1).

provider_outcome.error: Price: must be greater than or equal to €0,00.
provider_outcome.effect: The price check runs alongside the currency check (both messages come back) and names the limit in the target currency's format; a price of 0 is not refused for its value.

app_must: Check currency prices are 0 or more before sending them.

condition: currency_prices is sent as an empty list.

provider_outcome.error: {"currency_prices": "can't be blank"}

app_must: Send at least one currency price.

condition: A subscription to a priced product ($10) is created for a customer with no card on file and no payment_collection_method that takes none (this site's default collection needs a card).

provider_outcome.error: No payment method was on file for the $10.00 balance
provider_outcome.effect: No subscription is created; the message names the amount due.

app_must: Collect a payment method before subscribing, or send payment_collection_method remittance where the site allows it.

condition: A subscription is created with payment_collection_method remittance and no card, on this site where remittance is allowed.

provider_outcome.effect: It is active at once and the first period's price is put on balance_in_cents (1000 for a $10 product) with signup_revenue 0.00 and total_revenue_in_cents 0: nothing is collected.

app_must: Read balance_in_cents as the amount owed on a remittance subscription; do not show a new one as paid.

condition: A subscription is created with an empty body (no product and no customer).

provider_outcome.error: Product must be specified and be a valid product provided by the seller. / A Customer must be specified for the subscription to be valid.
provider_outcome.effect: Both messages come back together in the errors list.

app_must: Always send a product (product_handle or product_id) and a customer, and show every message in the errors list.

condition: The same createSubscription request (same customer and product, no uniqueness_token) is sent twice in a row or twice at the same moment.

provider_outcome.effect: Both calls return 201 and two active subscriptions exist for the customer, each with its own first-period balance.

app_must: Guard subscription creation yourself (check the customer's subscriptions or send a uniqueness_token) so a retry does not create a second subscription.

condition: A fractional quantity (0.5) is sent for a metered component whose allow_fractional_quantities is false (this site's API Calls component).

provider_outcome.effect: The usage is accepted and stored with quantity 0; the fraction is dropped without an error.

app_must: Round or reject fractional quantities yourself before reporting usage to a component without fractional quantities.
conflict: maxio-c4:createUsage.7: the docs say a decimal quantity on a component without fractional quantities is refused; the sandbox accepted 0.5 with 200 and stored 0; this record follows the sandbox.

condition: A usage is sent with an empty usage object (no quantity).

provider_outcome.error: {"usage": "can't be blank"}
provider_outcome.effect: No usage is recorded.

app_must: Always send a quantity with each usage.

condition: A family's products are listed without sort parameters right after a product was created in it.

provider_outcome.effect: The list starts with the family's oldest products (created 2026-11-04, in ascending order), so the product created a moment earlier is not at the top; the response was cut before showing whether it is listed.

app_must: Find a just-created product by its id or handle, or page to the end of the family list, not at its top.

condition: Usages of a subscription component are listed without sort parameters.

provider_outcome.effect: The newest usage comes first (descending id), including two usages with the same created_at.

app_must: Sort usages yourself if you need them oldest first, and do not assume the first item is the earliest report.

condition: A migration names the product and price point the subscription already has, including a second identical migration right after one succeeded.

provider_outcome.error: Cannot migrate to same product and same price point
provider_outcome.effect: Nothing changes; the repeated migration is refused, not ignored.

app_must: Compare the target with the subscription's current product and price point before migrating, and treat this 422 on a retry as done.

condition: A migration is sent with an empty migration object (no product_handle or product_id).

provider_outcome.error: Invalid Product

app_must: Always send the target product_handle or product_id.

condition: A plain migration (no proration fields) is requested for an on_hold subscription.

provider_outcome.error: This subscription is not eligible for a prorated migration
provider_outcome.effect: The subscription stays on hold on its old product.

app_must: Resume an on_hold subscription before migrating it, or change its product with updateSubscription.
conflict: maxio-c4:migrateSubscriptionProduct.11: the docs give this message when a prorated migration is requested; the sandbox returned it for a plain migration of an on_hold subscription; this record follows the sandbox.

condition: A migration is requested for a canceled subscription.

provider_outcome.error: Subscription in 'Canceled' state is not eligible for product migration
provider_outcome.effect: The subscription stays canceled on its old product.

app_must: Offer plan switching by migration only for active subscriptions; reactivate first if needed.

condition: Two identical migration requests for the same active subscription are sent at the same moment.

provider_outcome.error: The subscription cannot be migrated at this time.
provider_outcome.effect: The other call returns 200 and the subscription is migrated once (balance 1500).

app_must: On this 422, read the subscription to see whether the other migration went through before retrying.

condition: An active remittance subscription with a 1000 balance on a $10 product is migrated to a $15 product without preserve_period.

provider_outcome.effect: The product changes now, the period restarts at the migration moment (ends one month later), and balance_in_cents becomes 1500, not 2500.

app_must: Read the subscription after a migration for the new period dates and balance; do not add the new price to the old balance.

condition: A hold is requested for a subscription that is already on_hold (including a second hold right after the first) or is canceled.

provider_outcome.error: This subscription is not eligible to be put on hold.
provider_outcome.effect: The subscription keeps its state; the repeated hold is refused, not ignored.

app_must: Put only active subscriptions on hold, and treat this 422 after a retry as 'already on hold' once a read confirms it.

condition: Two identical hold requests for the same active subscription are sent at the same moment.

provider_outcome.error: This subscription is not eligible to be put on hold.
provider_outcome.effect: One returns 200 and puts the subscription on hold, the other gets this 422; both answers took about 20 seconds.

app_must: Send one hold per subscription at a time, allow a long wait, and read the subscription when one of the pair fails.

condition: automatically_resume_at is sent as yesterday's or today's date.

provider_outcome.error: Automatic resume date: must be at least 24 hours in the future.
provider_outcome.effect: The subscription stays active.

app_must: Offer resume dates at least 24 hours ahead.

condition: automatically_resume_at is sent as a date without a time (here 2031-11-10, five years ahead).

provider_outcome.effect: The date is accepted with no upper limit and stored as midnight in the site's time zone (2031-11-10T00:00:00+05:00).

app_must: Send a full date-time with an offset when the resume time of day matters; a bare date resumes at midnight site time.
conflict: maxio-c4:every-request.14: the docs say a date sent without a time means noon in the site's time zone; the sandbox stored this resume date as midnight; this record follows the sandbox.

condition: A reactivation is requested for a subscription that is active (including a second reactivation right after one succeeded) or on_hold.

provider_outcome.error: Cannot reactivate a subscription that is not marked "Canceled" or "Trial Ended".
provider_outcome.effect: The subscription keeps its state.

app_must: Offer reactivation only for canceled (or trial-ended) subscriptions, and resume an on_hold one instead.
conflict: maxio-c4:reactivateSubscription.1: the docs' message also allows "Unpaid"; the sandbox's 422 names only "Canceled" or "Trial Ended"; this record follows the sandbox.

condition: A canceled remittance subscription (no card) with a 1000 balance is reactivated with no body (no resume, no preserve_balance).

provider_outcome.effect: It goes active with a new period starting now and balance_in_cents becomes 2000: the old balance is kept and the new period's price is added on top.

app_must: Expect the old balance to remain after a reactivation and show the customer the full balance_in_cents.
conflict: maxio-c4:reactivateSubscription.7: the docs say that without preserve_balance the existing balance is cleared; the sandbox kept the 1000 and added 1000 for the new period; this record follows the sandbox.

condition: Two identical reactivation requests for the same canceled subscription are sent at the same moment.

provider_outcome.error: A reactivation is already being processed. Please wait a few seconds and then check the subscription status.
provider_outcome.effect: The other call returns 200; the subscription is reactivated and charged once (balance 2000, not 3000).

app_must: On this 422, wait a few seconds and read the subscription instead of retrying the reactivation.

condition: Two identical resume requests for the same on_hold subscription are sent at the same moment.

provider_outcome.error: Only subscriptions that are on hold can be resumed.
provider_outcome.effect: One returns 200 and the subscription is active, the other gets this 422.

app_must: Treat this 422 after a concurrent or retried resume as success once a read shows the subscription active.

condition: next_billing_at is sent as yesterday's or today's date.

provider_outcome.error: Next billing at must be in the future
provider_outcome.effect: The billing date does not change.

app_must: Offer only dates from tomorrow on for the next billing date.

condition: next_billing_at is sent as a date far ahead (2031-11-10, five years out) on an active monthly subscription.

provider_outcome.effect: It is accepted with no upper limit: current_period_ends_at and next_assessment_at both become 2031-11-10T12:00:00+05:00, so the current period stretches to five years.

app_must: Set your own upper limit on next billing dates; the server will stretch the current period to any future date.

condition: next_billing_at is changed on an on_hold or canceled subscription.

provider_outcome.error: 'Next Billing' cannot be changed for Subscriptions in 'on_hold' state (and 'canceled' state for a canceled one)
provider_outcome.effect: The billing date does not change.

app_must: Change the next billing date only on active subscriptions; resume or reactivate first.

condition: The same product_handle or next_billing_at update is sent again right after, or twice at the same moment.

provider_outcome.effect: Every call returns 200 with the same subscription; the repeat changes nothing more (updated_at stays, no further balance change).

app_must: Retry a failed product or billing-date update freely; it is safe to send twice.
